subject: Telemetry gate and trace-sampling agreement for private VPC export
messages:
From: Eric Shaw <eric@seculogix.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: obs-team@seculogix.com
Date: 2026-10-18T16:10:00Z
Subject: Telemetry gate: VPC log/trace export + sampling question

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this. We're getting our Private (VPC) deployment ready and have a couple of practical questions before we flip the switch on log/trace exports to our SIEM. High level: we want encrypted, authenticated delivery to our Splunk HEC cluster (FQDN: hec01.seculogix.net), deterministic firewall rules, and a sampling policy so we don't flood our retention budget.

Questions:
- Network: are we expected to open outbound to a set of IPs or FQDNs? We prefer FQDN allowlists but need guidance for our egress controls.
- Auth: does Redwood support mTLS for the forwarder -> HEC, or just token-based HEC? Any token rotation cadence recommended?
- Mapping: which Redwood fields map to Splunk event fields (uri, user_id, model_name, latency_ms)?
- Sampling: can we do prefix-based trace sampling (keep all /api/v1/infer requests at 20% and keep errors + p95 traces always)?
- Retention: what are your recommended retention windows for raw traces vs aggregated metrics in a private deployment?

Can you share the runbook/stub we should hand to our infra team so they can make firewall/ACL changes? Also include any PoLP guidance for token access.

--
Eric Shaw
Security Architect, SecuLogix
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Eric Shaw <eric@seculogix.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Telemetry gate: VPC log/trace export + sampling question

Hi Eric — thanks, this is exactly the right set of questions. Sending an initial plan below and attaching a short runbook and a sample sampling policy (see attachments). Happy to iterate after your infra team reviews.

Summary answers (short):
- Network: we recommend FQDN allowlist to your collector (hec01.seculogix.net) and a graceful fallback to an internal forwarder. We'll provide both FQDNs and a short-lived IP list for emergency firewall rules. Use outbound TLS (443) only.
- Auth: Redwood Private supports mTLS for forwarder connections and token-based HEC as a fallback. mTLS provides stronger assurance; token rotation every 30 days is a good default.
- Mapping: we provide a configurable field map. Default mapping:
  - redwood.request.path -> uri
  - redwood.user.id -> user_id
  - redwood.model -> model_name
  - redwood.latency.ms -> latency_ms
  - redwood.request_id -> _request_id (indexed)
- Sampling: we support prefix-based sampling and rule priorities. Out of the box: 100% for errors, 100% for traces with latency > p99, prefix rules (e.g., /api/v1/infer) can be sampled at X% (configurable). The attached sampling-policy-v1.yaml is an example you can adopt.
- Retention guidance (recommended):
  - Raw traces: 30 days full fidelity
  - Aggregated spans/metrics: 365 days (compressed/rollup)
  - Raw logs: 90 days (customers with compliance needs can extend)

Runbook highlights (attached PDF):
1) Firewall: outbound to hec01.seculogix.net:443 and telemetry-gateway.redwood-internal.net:443. Provide both FQDN and advisory short IP list (updated weekly).
2) Certificate exchange: for mTLS provide CA bundle and CSR format we accept; cert rotation every 90 days recommended for client certs.
3) Token: HEC token rotation policy: rotate on 30-day cadence, revoke previous token after confirmation. Use least-privilege token binding to a single collector endpoint.
4) Buffering/backpressure: forwarder will buffer locally up to configurable quota (default 2GB) and will retry with exponential backoff.

Next step: if this matches what you want, suggest a 30 min call with your infra + security to agree the ACLs and certificate exchange process.

Thanks,

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-telemetry-gate-runbook.pdf; sampling-policy-v1.yaml
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Eric Shaw <eric@seculogix.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T12:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Telemetry gate: VPC log/trace export + sampling question

Looping in a couple of operational items I want captured in the final runbook and evidence bundle (SOC2 audit friendliness):

- Retention ledger: please include sample retention-change request and ACL required to modify retention for raw traces (we should record who approved retention > default).
- Audit evidence: what logs do we produce when a token is rotated / revoked (timestamp, actor, request id)? Need to ship sample entries to SecuLogix for their SOC2 review.
- On-prem forwarder sizing: suggest we include guidance for disk buffer sizing (default 2GB -> recommended 10GB for customers with bursty traffic) and a suggested S3-compatible sink for emergency export.
- Encryption in transit: verify we list TLS v1.3 minimum and ciphers.

Eric: if you can confirm the retention windows Mina suggested that will let us finalize the evidence checklist.

Kimberly
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Eric Shaw <eric@seculogix.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Telemetry gate: VPC log/trace export + sampling question

Thanks — quick operational runbook notes from infra/serving side:

1) Egress topology: our private forwarder runs in-customer VPC as a sidecar (no public IP). It opens outbound TLS to your HEC collector. If your environment requires, we can route via a customer-managed NAT gateway and provide an IP list (weekly).
2) mTLS: to enable, we'll need a client cert PEM + chain from SecuLogix. We'll test in staging and provide a small validation tool (curl wrapper) to fetch a 200 from HEC with the cert.
3) Sampling policy: recommend two-tier model:
   - Tier A (critical paths): prefix match /api/v1/infer -> sample at 25% but always keep errors and p95+/p99
   - Tier B (control/metrics-heavy): sample at 1-5% for endpoints that produce high cardinality meta events
   - Head-based sampling for high-volume short-lived requests: drop after collecting a head sample window of N spans unless error or error-rate threshold trips.
4) Backpressure and buffer: default local buffer 2GB with configurable cap; when buffer > 80% we prioritize error traces and drop low-priority sampling.

I'll attach a short example kickstart config in the runbook (already in Mina's attachment). If you approve the retention windows Mina suggested, we'll produce the retention-change template and the audit log sample for token rotation.

Jonas
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
From: Eric Shaw <eric@seculogix.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Telemetry gate: VPC log/trace export + sampling question

Team — this looks good and aligned with our compliance needs. Confirming acceptance of the recommended retention windows: raw traces 30d, aggregated metrics 365d, raw logs 90d. We will plan to consume the runbook and request the mTLS cert chain by Friday (2026-10-23).

We also want the token-rotation audit sample in the evidence bundle; if you can include a short example entry (timestamp, actor, old_token_id, new_token_id, request_id) that will speed our SOC review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Let's pick the 30-min call tomorrow 10:30am PT to finalize ACLs.

--
Eric
Security Architect, SecuLogix
